patch.offer: TabPalette shows Chrome-style group chips in the tab bar after a one-time patch of VS Code. Enable it?
patch.confirm: Enable Chrome-style tab groups in the tab bar?
patch.confirmWhy: TabPalette draws group chips and colored group lines on VS Code's tab bar. VS Code has no API for that, so this adds a small script to VS Code's installation (workbench.html).
patch.confirmCorrupt: • VS Code may then say "Your Code installation appears to be corrupt". This is expected; choose "Don't Show Again".
patch.confirmUpdates: • VS Code updates replace the file; the extension offers to re-apply it.
patch.confirmUndo: • Run "Tab Groups: Disable Chrome-style Tab Groups" to undo it completely.
patch.enabled: TabPalette: enabled. Reload the window to see group chips in the tab bar.
patch.disabled: TabPalette: tab bar patch removed and VS Code's files restored. Reload the window to apply.
patch.updated: TabPalette: tab bar script updated. Reload the window to apply.
patch.removedByUpdate: TabPalette: a VS Code update removed the tab bar patch. Re-apply it?
patch.reapplied: TabPalette: re-applied. Reload the window to apply.
patch.noWorkbench: TabPalette: couldn't find VS Code's workbench.html under {0}. This VS Code build isn't supported.
patch.writeFailed: TabPalette: could not change VS Code's files. {0}
patch.noWriteAccess: VS Code is installed in a folder you cannot write to. Run VS Code as administrator once, run the command again, then restart normally.
